codes.total_rationale: All three items map onto behavioural-addiction / ICD-11 gaming-disorder-type criteria. Item 1 is about AI use getting priority and throwing life balance off (salience/conflict). Item 2 is about using AI more than intended (loss of control). Item 3 is about continuing to use AI despite harm (negative consequences). No item asks about relying on AI for tasks or for emotional support, so the whole index is T1.
quoted_items: Using AI chatbots noticeably changes the balance between different areas of my life (e.g., study, relationships, rest).
I sometimes use an AI chatbot more often than I originally intended.
I sometimes continue using an AI chatbot even though I know it is not good for me (e.g., it takes time, distracts me, lowers my mood).
codes.note: Ad hoc 3-item index from R1053 with no subscales. The authors report it as a mean symptom-severity index and say it is not a homogeneous latent scale, so expect low internal consistency.

codes.total_rationale: All 3 items map onto behavioural-addiction components. Interference with study/work is conflict or negative consequences. Uneasiness when generative AI cannot be used is withdrawal. Difficulty controlling use is loss of control. No item is about relying on AI for tasks or for emotional support, so this is a uniform addiction-type scale.
quoted_items: Using generative AI sometimes interferes with my other activities (such as study and work).
I feel a bit uneasy when I cannot use generative AI.
I find it difficult to control my using generative AI.
codes.note: Single total score (α = .80), no subscales. All 3 declared items were printed in R3484 (Zhou & Zhang, 2024). Development paper and adaptation source are not available.
